[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
John was born about 1780. He was the natural son of [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]]. John Glasgow died at some point before September 1817; he appears to have owned a metalwork business, owning five blacksmiths, two coppersmiths, a carpenter, four labourers as well as three female house servants and five children. By 1822, two of the women and all five of the children had been purchased by the Montgreenan plantation. John's "housekeeper" (and common-law wife?), [[Theobalds-120|Amelia]], inherited enslaved people from John Glasgow for the term of her natural life: in March 1817 she registered ownership of Mary, age 25, a house servant and four children Adam (age 7), Eve (age 5), Peter (age 3), and James (age 1). Adam and his siblings may have the children of John and Amelia.

== Reseach Notes ==
* [[Glasgow-1076|Robert Glasgow of Montgreenan]] had at least three natural children. A trust deed of 1803 reads as follows:<blockquote>To my reputed natural mulatto son John and the lawful heirs of his body, I leave the sum of two hundred pounds sterling. To my reputed natural daughter Emilia and the lawful heirs of her body, I leave the sum of five hundred pounds sterling. To Robert, the reputed natural son of my late brother James and the lawful heirs etc... I leave the lawful sum of one hundred pounds sterling. To James the reputed natural son of my said brother etc.... the sum of fifty pounds sterling.</blockquote>
* Robert bequeathed the estates of Montgreenan and Sans Souci in St Vincent to his youngest natural daughter Anne and her husband Robert Robertson of Gunsgreen House, Eyemouth (both q.v.). The legacy was made conditional upon Robert assuming the name Glasgow.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1076]] is assessed at 99% (proved). Robert of Montgreenan’s retained 1803 trust clause expressly calls John his reputed natural son and leaves him a named legacy. The distinctive Montgreenan/St Vincent family identifies the selected Robert, separately from the same deed’s nephews and other children.

Confident 99% as the deed’s acknowledged son; John’s household, maternity and later estate details remain separately qualified.

Next useful test: Inspect the trust’s original John clause when available.

Source basis already held: [https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146643739 “Dr Robert Glasgow” (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/lbs/person/view/2146643739), Legacies of British Slavery, UCL; citing SC6/44/4, T71/493 pp. 591–592 and T71/495 p. 54; consulted 10 September 2026.]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.
